key.lesson: a lesson, from easy to hard subject
slot.name: {day}, lesson {period}
hint.dsatur: Step 1 builds a first timetable. The lesson with the fewest free places is always placed first: the number beside each class is that count for its tightest lesson. Hover a number to see the lesson. Press One step or Play.
hint.annealing: Step 2 improves the timetable by trying random changes. Colour shows how hard the subject is, a dark corner marks a lesson in a poor place. Press One step to follow one change, or Play.
hint.kempe: Step 3 adds a smarter change: a chain of lessons that swap between two times together. Press One step to see one chain, or Play.
trouble.0: the same subject twice this day
trouble.1: an easy lesson in the first half of the day
trouble.2: a hard lesson in the second half of the day
trouble.3: at a time its teacher asked to avoid
dsatur.scoring: +{gap} for a gap in the class day, +{same} for the same subject twice a day, +{load} per lesson already that day
dsatur.pick.title: Whose turn?

dsatur.pick.text.one: {lesson} goes next: it has {n} free place left, and no waiting lesson has fewer. If it waited, others could take its last places. Green dots are its free places.{closed}
dsatur.pick.text.other: {lesson} goes next: it has {n} free places left, and no waiting lesson has fewer. If it waited, others could take its last places. Green dots are its free places.{closed}

dsatur.pick.closed: Red crosses: its teacher is busy then.
dsatur.judge.title: Which place is best?
dsatur.judge.text: Each free place gets penalty points: {scoring}. The fewest points win: {slot}.
dsatur.none.title: No place left
dsatur.none.text: {lesson} has no free place, so it stays unplaced. Step 2 repairs it.
dsatur.place.title: Place it
dsatur.place.text: {lesson} takes {slot}. That time is now closed for its class and its teacher{lost}.

dsatur.place.lost.one: , so {n} waiting lesson loses a place
dsatur.place.lost.other: , so {n} waiting lessons lose a place

dsatur.running: Placing lessons, the one with the fewest free places first: {placed} of {total}.

dsatur.done.broken.one: , but {n} rule is broken (red crosses{unplaced})
dsatur.done.broken.other: , but {n} rules are broken (red crosses{unplaced})

dsatur.done.text.one: {placed}{rules}. Still, {n} lesson (dark corner) sits in a poor place, and the timetable costs {cost} penalty points. Step 2 lowers that.
dsatur.done.text.other: {placed}{rules}. Still, {n} lessons (dark corner) sit in a poor place, and the timetable costs {cost} penalty points. Step 2 lowers that.

dsatur.note.next: {places}: the fewest of all waiting lessons, so it goes next
anneal.title.build: The blockers move the other way
cost.classClash: class has two lessons at once
cost.teacherClash: teacher in two classes at once
cost.misplaced: hard lesson late or easy one early
cost.dayImbalance: uneven number of lessons per day
anneal.formula.chance: chance to keep a worse change = e<sup>−Δ / T</sup>
anneal.formula.legend: Δ is how many penalty points worse the change is, T is the temperature.
anneal.formula.cooling: It cools from {start} to {end} over the run. Right now:
anneal.heatHint: a change {points} points worse is kept with chance {chance}
anneal.running: Trying random changes: {done} of {total}. Penalty now {cost}. The cooler it gets, the fewer worse changes are kept.
anneal.poor: Lessons in a poor place (dark corner): {before} → {after}.

anneal.broken.one: No valid timetable was found: {n} rule is still broken (red crosses). The school may be impossible as it is set up, or this search did not find the way. Penalty {before} → {after}.
anneal.broken.other: No valid timetable was found: {n} rules are still broken (red crosses). The school may be impossible as it is set up, or this search did not find the way. Penalty {before} → {after}.

anneal.done.next: {summary} Step 3 adds Kempe chains to go lower.
anneal.done.rival: {summary} Without chains the same number of attempts ends at {cost}: {comparison}.
anneal.compare.higher: on this school the chains did not help ({share} higher)
anneal.compare.same: about the same on this school
anneal.hop.first: {lesson} is in the way, so it moves the other way, to {to}.
anneal.hop.next: There it bumps into {lesson} ({why}), which has to move too.
anneal.stuck: {lesson} wants to move to {to}. But {clash}: a plain move would be a clash (red cross).
anneal.closed: Nobody else is in the way. All {n} lessons swap between {from} and {to} at once, so no clash appears.
anneal.price.text: The penalty of the whole timetable would go from {before} to {after}: {change}.{why}
anneal.verdict.always: {how}. Rule: a change that is not worse is always kept.
anneal.verdict.worse: Worse by {points} points. Rule: a worse change is kept only by chance, and the chance shrinks when the change is worse and when the temperature is lower. Here, at temperature {temperature}, the chance is {chance}.
anneal.dice.label: chance {chance}
anneal.dice.green: the random draw (black mark) fell in the green part: {outcome}
anneal.dice.red: the random draw (black mark) fell in the red part: {outcome}
wizard.create: Create the school and build its timetable
grades.language.hint: State schools in Kazakhstan teach either in Kazakh or in Russian. The choice changes the curriculum and how hard two subjects count: here {language} is the language of instruction and counts as easier ({easy} points), {other} is the second language and counts as harder ({hard} points).
grades.title: Which grades does your school have?
grades.text: Press a grade to add or remove it. Each grade follows the national curriculum for classes taught in {language}.
classes.shifts.hint: Many schools in Kazakhstan do not have enough rooms and teach in two shifts. With two shifts you choose for every grade whether it studies in the morning (lessons 1–8) or in the afternoon (lessons 9–16). Teachers work in both shifts, and a teacher whose day is torn between the shifts costs penalty points.
classes.shifts.lost: All your grades are in the same shift now, so the school stays one-shift.
classes.title: How many classes in each grade?
classes.split: Split each class into two groups for {subjects}
teachers.title: How many teachers for each subject?
teachers.text: The numbers are a suggestion of about 24 lessons a week per teacher. Fewer teachers means more lessons for each.
links.title: Which classes does each teacher take?
links.text: Lessons are shared out evenly to start with. Press a class to give it to that teacher: they then teach the subject in that class. Subjects with a single teacher are not listed.
links.none: Every subject has a single teacher, so there is nothing to choose. Add teachers on the previous step to share classes between them.
preferences.title: When can each teacher not work?
preferences.text.day: Every day has three parts. Press a part to close it for that teacher. Close all three for a full day off.
preferences.text.shift: Every shift has three parts. Press a part to close it for that teacher, close all of them for a full day off. A teacher only gets the shifts in which they have lessons.
summary.text: Your school: taught in {language}, {classes} classes, {lessons} lessons a week, {teachers} teachers
summary.text.shifts: Your school: taught in {language}, two shifts, {classes} classes, {lessons} lessons a week, {teachers} teachers
verdict.impossible.title: No valid timetable can exist for this school.
verdict.impossible.text: Add teachers or reopen some of their times. You can still build it to see where it breaks: lessons that do not fit stay red.
verdict.tight.title: A timetable may exist, but it will be hard to find.
verdict.tight.text: If rules stay broken at the end of the run, no valid timetable was found.
verdict.good.title: Nothing rules a timetable out.
verdict.good.text: Only the run shows whether a valid timetable is really found: this check cannot prove that one exists.
verdict.overloaded: Teacher {teacher} has {load} lessons a week but only {free} lesson times when they can teach.
verdict.nearlyFull: Teacher {teacher} is nearly full: {load} lessons in {free} possible times.
